symptom: A microflow calling a consumed REST operation with a path parameter (`send rest request Mod.RC.Op with ($id = …)`) makes the project **impossible to open** — mxbuild aborts with `The type cache does not contain a type with qualified name Microflows$ParameterMapping` from `StreamingBsonUnitReader`
cause: Both writers hardcoded `Microflows$ParameterMapping` as the `$Type` of each entry in `Microflows$RestOperationCallAction.ParameterMappings`. **No such Mendix type exists.** `generated/metamodel` is the arbiter — `MicroflowsRestOperationCallAction.ParameterMappings` is `[]*MicroflowsRestOperationParameterMapping` — so the storage name is `Microflows$RestOperationParameterMapping`. The sibling `QueryParameterMappings` was already correct, which is why only path parameters trip it
insight: A STORAGE-NAME OVERRIDE in the `$Type` sense, and the most dangerous shape of it: the failure is at **load**, before any check, so `mx check` never reaches the model and reports the exception instead of an error list — and `mxcli check` and `exec` both accept it happily. **Patch the list-marker registration as well as the `newElem`**, or the codec decodes under the old name. Found only by trying to BOOT an app (`run --local`), not by any static gate — the same lesson as the inline-mapping paths above: when a construct's symptom is "the runtime does the wrong thing", the runtime is the only honest test. Repro: any microflow with `send rest request … with (…)`; covered by `mdl-examples/bug-tests/rest-inline-mapping-paths.mdl`'s companion runtime probe. Reported indirectly via mxcli-rest FINDINGS #36's repro
